meta.titre: Pollination and Fertilization: from Pollen Grain to Seed
meta.sous_theme: Pollination, fertilization and what the flower becomes

sections.contenu_markdown: On a farm near Mbouda, a farmer watches bees move from blossom to blossom in his orange trees. A few weeks later, small green fruits begin to swell. Not far away, a field of maize fills its cobs with grains, yet hardly an insect is seen there. Both crops depend on the same two events: pollination, then fertilization. Biology papers at the GCE often ask you to tell insect-pollinated flowers from wind-pollinated ones, and to say what the parts of a flower turn into afterwards.

items: A flower has male parts (stamens, each with an anther) and a female part (the carpel, made of stigma, style and ovary).
A gamete is a sex cell, and in sexual reproduction a male gamete fuses with a female gamete.
The ovary of a flower contains one or more ovules.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Pollination
**Pollination** is the transfer of pollen grains from an anther to a stigma. In **self-pollination** the pollen reaches a stigma of the same flower or of another flower on the same plant. In **cross-pollination** it reaches a flower on a different plant of the same species. The two main agents are insects and wind.

### Insect-pollinated and wind-pollinated flowers
| Feature | Insect-pollinated flower | Wind-pollinated flower |
|---|---|---|
| Petals | Large and brightly coloured | Small and dull, or absent |
| Scent and nectar | Present, to attract and reward insects | Absent |
| Anthers | Inside the flower, firmly attached | Hang outside on long filaments, so the wind shakes them |
| Pollen | Smaller amount, sticky or rough so that it clings to insects | Very large amount, small, light and smooth so that the wind carries it |
| Stigma | Small and sticky, inside the flower | Large and feathery, hanging outside to catch pollen from the air |

### Fertilization
**Fertilization** is the fusion of a male gamete nucleus with the female gamete nucleus (the egg cell). It happens in four steps:
1. A pollen grain lands on a suitable stigma and grows a **pollen tube**.
2. The tube grows down through the style towards the ovary, carrying the male nucleus.
3. The tube enters an ovule through a small opening called the **micropyle**.
4. The male nucleus fuses with the egg nucleus and forms a **zygote**.

### After fertilization
| Part | What it becomes |
|---|---|
| Fertilized ovule | Seed |
| Zygote | Embryo inside the seed |
| Ovary | Fruit |
| Ovary wall | Wall of the fruit |
| Petals, stamens, style and stigma | Wither and fall off |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to differentiate between, compare, or give the differences between two kinds of flower
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write feature by feature, naming both flowers in each point, and add the reason when you can. Example: the wind-pollinated flower has a large feathery stigma, whereas the insect-pollinated flower has a small sticky stigma inside the flower. The feathery stigma gives a large surface for catching pollen from the air. Do not list the features of only one flower.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When options or statements mix the two processes
variantes.contenu_markdown: Pollination moves pollen between flower parts and comes first. Fertilization is the fusion of nuclei and takes place inside the ovule. Pollen can land on a stigma without any fertilization following.

variantes.nom: Which part becomes the fruit or the seed?
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a description is matched to a heading, for example 'it becomes the seed'
variantes.contenu_markdown: Match the part to the product: ovule to seed, ovary to fruit. The flower as a whole does not become the fruit.

sections.enonce_markdown: A student examines a flower with no scent. Its anthers hang outside the flower on long, thin filaments, and its large feathery stigmas also hang outside. (a) State how this flower is pollinated and give three features that support your answer. (b) Describe what happens between the landing of a pollen grain on the stigma and the formation of the seed.

etapes.action: Read the command words: 'state' needs a short answer and 'describe' needs a sequence.
etapes.justification: This tells you to give the agent, then features with reasons, then an ordered series of events.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Part (a): agent plus three features. Part (b): ordered events.

etapes.action: Identify the agent from the clues.
etapes.justification: No scent, hanging anthers and feathery stigmas outside the flower are the signs of a flower that does not use animals.

etapes.action: Pick three features and give a reason for each.
etapes.justification: A feature without a reason earns fewer marks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Hanging anthers: the wind shakes the pollen out. Feathery stigma: large surface that catches pollen from the air. No scent: there is no need to attract insects.

etapes.justification: The events must follow the real sequence.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Pollen grain grows a pollen tube, the tube grows down the style, it enters the ovule through the micropyle, and the male nucleus fuses with the egg nucleus.

etapes.justification: The question ends with the formation of the seed.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The zygote forms an embryo, the ovule becomes the seed, and the ovary becomes the fruit.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** (a) The flower is wind-pollinated. Its anthers hang outside, so the wind can shake out the pollen. Its stigmas are large and feathery, so they catch pollen from the air. It has no scent, because it does not need to attract insects. (b) The pollen grain grows a pollen tube down the style to the ovary. The tube enters the ovule through the micropyle, and the male nucleus fuses with the egg nucleus to form a zygote. The zygote develops into an embryo, the ovule becomes the seed and the ovary becomes the fruit.

items.erreur_markdown: Pollination is when the male gamete joins the female gamete.
items.pourquoi_faux: That describes fertilization. Pollination only moves the pollen to the stigma.
items.correction_markdown: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma. Fertilization is the later fusion of the male and female nuclei.

items.erreur_markdown: The pollen tube carries the whole pollen grain down to the ovule.
items.pourquoi_faux: The tube grows out of the pollen grain, which stays on the stigma. The tube carries the male nucleus.
items.correction_markdown: The pollen tube grows down the style and delivers the male nucleus to the egg cell in the ovule.

items.erreur_markdown: After fertilization the whole flower becomes the fruit.
items.pourquoi_faux: Petals, stamens, style and stigma wither. Only the ovary and its contents are kept.
items.correction_markdown: The ovary becomes the fruit and the ovules become seeds.

items.erreur_markdown: Wind-pollinated flowers have bright petals and sweet nectar to attract the wind.
items.pourquoi_faux: The wind cannot be attracted. Bright petals and nectar are for insects, and they would only get in the way of wind pollination.
items.correction_markdown: Wind-pollinated flowers have small dull petals, no nectar, exposed anthers and large feathery stigmas.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Define pollination. (b) State one difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination. (c) Name two agents of pollination.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from an anther to a stigma.** (b) In self-pollination the pollen lands on a stigma of the same plant, while in cross-pollination it lands on a flower of a different plant of the same species. (c) **Insects and wind.**

items.enonce_markdown: A flower has large scented petals and a small sticky stigma inside the flower. Its pollen grains are few and spiny. (a) Say how it is pollinated. (b) Give three reasons. (c) Name one reward that attracts the visitors.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **By insects.** (b) Large scented petals attract insects. A sticky stigma inside the flower collects pollen from the body of a visitor. Few spiny grains cling to the insect, whereas wind-pollinated flowers produce very large amounts of light smooth pollen. (c) **Nectar.**

items.enonce_markdown: A gardener removes the anthers from some young flower buds of a plant before they open. He covers half of those buds with fine bags and leaves the other half uncovered. The flowers are insect-pollinated. Predict what happens to each set and explain.
items.solution_markdown: Bagged buds: with no anthers there is no pollen of their own, and the bag keeps insects out, so no pollen reaches the stigma. There is no pollination, no fertilization, and so **no fruit or seed forms**. Uncovered buds: they have no pollen of their own, but insects can bring pollen from other plants. This is cross-pollination, so fertilization can follow, and **the ovaries can develop into fruits containing seeds**.

items_markdown: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma. Fertilization is the fusion of the male nucleus with the egg nucleus.
Insect-pollinated flowers have large coloured petals, scent, nectar, sticky or rough pollen and a stigma inside the flower.
Wind-pollinated flowers have small dull petals, no scent, hanging anthers, large amounts of light pollen and large feathery stigmas.
The pollen tube grows down the style and enters the ovule through the micropyle, carrying the male nucleus.
After fertilization the ovule becomes the seed and the ovary becomes the fruit.
